html:
The Chandelas ruled Jejakabhukti, today's Bundelkhand in central India, from the 9th century to the early 14th. Their forts were Kalinjar and Mahoba.

They began as vassals of the Gurjara-Pratiharas and broke free in the 10th century under Yashovarman and Dhanga, when they were among the strongest kings of the north. The Khajuraho temples, built mostly between 950 and 1050, are their great work, famous for their carved figures.

Vidyadhara stood up to Mahmud of Ghazni in the early 11th century and kept his kingdom. In 1182 Prithviraj Chauhan defeated King Paramardi. In 1203 Qutb ud-Din Aibak took Kalinjar for the rising Delhi Sultanate, and the Chandelas survived only as local rulers until the early 1300s.
sum: The Chandelas ruled Jejakabhukti, today's Bundelkhand in central India, from the 9th century to the early 14th. Their forts were Kalinjar and Mahoba.
